agenda_text:

  conduct a Special Meeting, at the following time and place, and will
  address the agenda listed below:

  CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

can view this meeting through live webcast at www.beverlyhills.org/live and on BH

Hall.

minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Room 280A
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  The Beverly Hills City Council Liaison /
  Finance and Audit Committee

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Tuesday, July 9, 2024
  3:35 PM
MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  July 9, 2024 / 3:35 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Mayor Lester Friedman, Councilmember Mary Wells, City Treasurer
  Howard Fisher, City Manager Nancy Hunt-Coffey, Assistant City Manager
  Ryan Gohlich, Director of Finance Jeff Muir, Assistant Director of Finance
  Tatiana Szerwinski, Planning & Research Analyst Sivan Levin, &
  Executive Assistant Vanessa Catullo

  1) PUBLIC COMMENT

  Members of the public were given the opportunity to directly address the Committee on
  any item listed on the agenda.
  None.

  2) DISCUSSION AND DIRECTION TO REVIEW COST REDUCTION AND REVENUE
  ENHANCEMENT OPPORTUNTIES.

  The Director of Finance began the discussion by informing the Committee on the updated
  forecast summary presented to City Council as part of the budget adoption process, which
  projects significant operating deficits through fiscal year 2028-29 9 (excluding public
  benefit contributions). The budget was approved by Council with the understanding that
  additional actions are required to limit or avoid these future deficits.

  The City Manager provided the following proposals which may result in improved
  efficiencies and/or possible reductions in expenditures.
  •  Commission Standardization Liaison
  o  Consider any further consolidation/changes to commissions.
  •  RDC/Special Events Liaison
  o  Consider the totality of events offered by the City and determine if any
  changes, reductions, or eliminations are warranted.
   CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Room 280A
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  The Beverly Hills City Council Liaison /
  Finance and Audit Committee

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Tuesday, July 9, 2024
  3:35 PM
  •  Social Services Ad Hoc
  o  Consider overlaps in Community Assistance Grant Funds and other City
  services considering recent investments in housing for the homeless and
  consolidation of social services in the Fire Department.
  •  Community Security Ad Hoc
  o  Consider the role of the Ambassadors and private security and whether
  there is overlap or a change in responsibilities.
  •  Litigation Liaison
  o  Consider lines of insurance to consider the possibility of pooled coverage
  and whether any reductions can be made without significantly
  compromising coverage.
  •  CVB/Chamber Liaison
  o  Conduct cost benefit analysis of work performed by partner agencies.

The Director of Finance suggested the committee review the major expenditure areas by
department.
  •  Contractual/consultant services
  •  Travel and training
  •  Supplies
  •  Overtime

The Director of Finance shared the summary of recommendations from the Blue Ribbon
Committee.
  •  Consider a sales tax (transactions and use tax) increase.
  •  Consider a transient occupancy tax (TOT) increase.
  •  Expedite real estate leasing processes to maximize returns.
  •  Review business tax license categories and basis for tax calculations.
  •  Consider future debt issuance/bonds.
   CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Room 280A
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  The Beverly Hills City Council Liaison /
  Finance and Audit Committee

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Tuesday, July 9, 2024
  3:35 PM
  •  Consider reviewing project planning and permitting processes.
  •  Consider special assessment districts.
  •  Consider public-private partnerships.
  •  Consider parking revenue recapture.
  •  Consider recouping development costs associated with impacts on public
  infrastructure and services.

  Mayor Friedman, Councilmember Wells, and City Treasurer Howard Fisher provided
  direction and action items for reductions in expenditures.

  •  Establish the City’s priorities for the next year and beyond to focus on what areas
  need more attention and which have too much attention. Prioritization would help
  to understand what we as a City are not able to accomplish due to current spending
  patterns.
  •  Work with departments to make sure their work plans align with updated City
  priorities.
  •  Start considering the City Manager’s proposals for reductions in expenditures
  provided at the beginning of the discussion.
  •  Contemplate zero based budgeting in certain areas over a five year period.
  •  Establish a timeline for setting priorities and for implementing expenditure
  reductions  and  simultaneously  working  on  revenue  enhancement
  recommendation options, so if needed, they can be implemented timely.
  •  Revisit free parking in the City.

3) ADJOURNMENT

  Date/Time: July 9, 2024 / 4:28 PM
